summary: One-line fix wraps the Subs expression in \left(...\right), correctly resolving the reported mis-parenthesizing; minimal and on-target. Only downside is unconditional wrapping adds redundant parens around atomic expressions (e.g. Subs(x,(x,),(1,))), a cosmetic imperfection not worth blocking.

issues.description: Parens added unconditionally regardless of expression precedence, so a single atom or already-grouped expr gets redundant parentheses (e.g. Subs(x,(x,),(1,)) -> \left(x\right)). A precedence-aware wrap would be cleaner, but over-parenthesizing is never incorrect output.
Always-wrap is a slightly blunt approach versus checking precedence of the inner expression, but it is simple, robust, and produces valid LaTeX in all cases.
